teams.heading: Fiji Latui down to 12 men as Ireland XV run in nine tries
teams.body: Fiji's second-string Latui side saw their discipline unravel against an Ireland XV in Cork on Friday night, three yellow cards in quick succession leaving them with 12 men for a spell. Isaia Lotawa went first for a no-arms tackle that conceded a penalty try, before tighthead Mesake Doge and Apisalome Kuruisaqila followed for a high tackle and a deliberate knock-on. Doge was then sent off with a second yellow for collapsing a scrum moments after returning. Ireland ran in nine tries to win 62-12, by RTÉ's count.

lead.why: The only new Fiji event in the coverage: the second-string Latui side's card-strewn defeat to an Ireland XV.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje calls All Blacks clash a 'massive game for England'
teams.body: England went into the Hillary Shield Test at Twickenham with a Nations Championship final place in play and an uncomfortable record to answer. The Guardian noted that in head coach Steve Borthwick's era they had won just four of their past 20 Tests against South Africa, New Zealand, France, Ireland and Scotland. Captain Maro Itoje called it "a massive game for England" and expected a furious reaction from an All Blacks side beaten by Wales the week before.

lead.why: It is the freshest England-centred story not already run: the captain's framing of the New Zealand Test and England's poor record against top sides.

teams.heading: Rugbyrama warns Galthié's France must back up Springbok win against Argentina
teams.body: Rugbyrama's Jérémy Fadat argues that France's historic weakness is stringing top-level performances together over several weeks. Head coach Fabien Galthié has long flagged that failing with his line "Nous sommes des Latins." Fadat points to the 2026 Six Nations, which France won yet finished in a slump. The Argentina test comes eight days after the 21-19 win over South Africa, and victory would put Antoine Dupont's side into the Nations Championship final at Twickenham the following weekend.

lead.why: It is the freshest France-centred item that has not already led, and it ties Galthié's own warning to what a win over Argentina would earn.

teams.heading: Gus McCarthy, Daniel Ryan score twice as Ireland XV rout Fiji Latui
teams.body: Ireland's second-string XV ran in nine tries against a Fiji Latui side that imploded in Cork on Friday, picking up four yellow cards and a red in the first half and briefly playing with 12 men. Captain McCarthy and Connacht's Ryan both finished with two, while out-half Joey Carbery set up the fourth-minute opener and later dived under the posts. Paul Boyle withdrew late from the bench with a neck issue, replaced by Scott Penny, and Eoin de Buitléar was sin-binned for a hip-drop tackle.

lead.why: The Ireland XV's nine-try win over Fiji Latui is the freshest Ireland result, and it moves on from Thursday's captaincy edition.

teams.heading: Quesada handed Domingo Miotti his Italy debut at fly-half against Fiji
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada said the Montpellier No. 10's place in Saturday's test in Udine had been planned from the start, with Paolo Garbisi and Tommy Allan both told. He weighed starting Garbisi or Allan at 10 with Miotti on the bench. Injuries to wings Lynagh, Faissal, Pani and Trulla instead pushed Ange Capuozzo to the wing and Allan to full-back. The only other change from the Argentina defeat was Alessandro Ortombina starting in place of Federico Ruzza, with Quesada naming him lineout leader.

lead.why: Quesada's reasoning for Miotti's debut and the Ortombina call is the selection story, and earlier editions covered Nicotera, Miotti's back-story and off-field visits instead.

teams.heading: Scotland U20 edge Ireland 31-29 in Cork as Hamish Mather seals win
teams.body: Scotland U20 survived five Irish tries on Friday night, as Fergus Pringle's side won on accuracy off the kicking tee. Glasgow Hawks wing Rory Caldwell scored twice. Edinburgh academy players James Dalrymple, Christian Lindsay and Rory McHaffie also crossed, and Harry Clark landed three conversions. Ireland's Paul Neary, the St Mary's out-half, sent a late conversion to level the scores wide. After the clock went red, replacement Hamish Mather ripped the ball free to secure the result.

lead.why: Scotland U20's win in Cork is the only fresh Scotland event; the other items are broadcast logistics or stories already run.

teams.heading: Tomos Williams credits the Prem for Wales players' growing confidence
teams.body: Saracens scrum-half Tomos Williams, one of nine England-based players in the Wales XV named for Saturday's test against Australia, told BBC Sport Wales that moving to England showed him English players were "a lot more confident than us." He pointed to Aaron Wainwright, captain Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan as examples of recent movers. Flanker Morgan joined Gloucester from Ospreys in the summer and was named Prem player of the month in October.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi accuses Montpellier of breaking Justo Piccardo workload deal before France
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi said on Friday that centre Justo Piccardo's absence from the side to face France was forced on the Pumas, not chosen. He said Piccardo had played 11 weeks in a row and that his GPS numbers had dropped against Italy, pointing to fatigue. Contepomi accused Montpellier's director of rugby Bernard Laporte and manager Joan Caudullo of breaking an agreement, leaving Argentina to manage the player's workload over the past fortnight. Lucio Cinti was named at outside centre in his place.

teams.heading: Every Wallabies match at home World Cup confirmed free on Nine
teams.body: Nine Entertainment will show half of the 52 matches at next year's men's Rugby World Cup free on its TV channels and its 9Now streaming service, according to Rugby World's broadcaster guide. Every Wallabies fixture is among them. The rest of the expanded 24-team tournament, played across Australia, goes to Stan Sport, which also carries the Wallabies' 2026 season. Stan Sport packages start at $20 per month on top of a basic $9.99 Stan subscription.

lead.why: The Liam Wright story ran yesterday, so this is the strongest new Australia item: how fans at home will watch the Wallabies at their own World Cup.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones rebuilds Japan's front row in nine changes after Twickenham
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones replaced his entire front row for Saturday's Nations Championship test against Scotland at Murrayfield. He named Sojiro Otsuka, Kenji Sato and Ryosuke Iwaihara after the 78-15 defeat by England at Twickenham a week earlier. OnRugby counted nine changes in all. Shinya Komura took the No. 10 jersey and Charlie Lawrence and Jisu Lee formed a new centre pairing, while Warner Dearns and Naoto Saito shared the captaincy.

teams.heading: Jordie Barrett says All Blacks drifted from their DNA before Dave Rennie
teams.body: Speaking on The Rugby Pod with former Wales fly-half Dan Biggar, All Blacks inside centre Jordie Barrett said the side 'probably went away from the All Black DNA, which is trying to play fast, moving the ball, using our athletes' under Scott Robertson, Rennie's predecessor, whose team leaned on territory and kicking. Barrett credited head coach Dave Rennie with 'challenging our thinking and our work ethic and our ability to be brave with the ball,' while insisting structure and forward dominance still matter.

lead.why: It is the top new story about the All Blacks themselves and has not been run, unlike the Kirk and Mo'unga threads.

teams.heading: James While backs three of Rassie Erasmus's 17 Paris knee-drop complaints
teams.body: Going back through all 17 knee-drops from the 19-21 defeat in Paris, Planet Rugby columnist James While rated three nailed-on penalties and four more as could-go-either-way. He concedes the Springboks had every right to feel aggrieved. He also sides with head coach Rassie Erasmus on access: under World Rugby's new protocols, a coach may meet the referee before a Test only if both coaches agree. He still holds that publicly accusing officials of match-fixing is the one line nobody crosses. Erasmus questioned whether referees were involved in match-fixing, and those comments earned him a six-match ban.

lead.why: The Stick-Prendergast story has already run, and this is the freshest South Africa angle: a critic of Erasmus concedes part of the Springboks' Paris grievance.
